mechanism: A query string is split into tokens. A word list of brands, sports and OSM tag names decides what to search for, and a geocoder (Photon) decides where. Relations like near, between, along and 100 m from are then compiled into Overpass QL and run on a custom Overpass engine. No language model is involved, so the same query always gives the same result.
claim: Deterministic natural-language search over OpenStreetMap that handles stacked queries such as bridges over the Danube 50 km from Novi Sad.
verdict_question: Of 15 plain-English place queries, how many does the HippoMaps parser (GPL, public repo) turn into valid Overpass QL that returns at least one result from a public Overpass endpoint?
probe_title: HippoMaps query parser: does it turn 15 plain-English place queries into Overpass QL that returns results?
one_line: HippoMaps turns plain-English place searches into OpenStreetMap queries with a word list and a geocoder, no language model, so the answer is repeatable.
idea_why: A tag word list plus a geocoder is a well-bounded way to turn natural language into structured queries without a model.
breakdown: Clone the public repo and find the query parser module. Feed it a fixed list of 15 queries of rising complexity, capture the Overpass QL it emits, and run each against a public Overpass endpoint. Score each as valid, empty or error. The Photon geocoder is also public and keyless. Anyone using this later would extend the word list for a new domain such as car-related POIs or open data sets.

mechanism: For each reported agent incident, the framework rebuilds the scene offline and builds a matched control that lacks only the blamed cause. Agents then run on both versions, so the cause is tested by the difference in how often the mistake happens. A warning after each tool output that names the hazard and its consequence was tested against a same-length note that did not name it.
claim: Reproduced the reported harm in 89% of 108 incidents; five models made the mistake in 18% to 33% of runs against at most 1% in controls.
why_not_testable: It needs model answers across several agents and there is no local LLM tonight.
needs: A model runner for repeated agent trials.
one_line: A paper rebuilds real agent disasters with and without the blamed cause: most had no attacker, and a warning naming the hazard cut harm.
idea_why: The matched-control design is sound, but the effect size comes from the authors' own replications.
breakdown: Take an incident report, write the environment as a small sandbox (a database shared with the live site, say), and write a twin with the cause removed. Run an agent on both a number of times and compare the mistake rates. Then add the hazard-naming warning after tool output and measure again. A person would do the incident-to-sandbox rebuild, which is the hard part to script.

mechanism: The agent loop and its sandbox run on the same long-lived VM per team, so there is no remote sandbox call per step. Sessions are isolated as git worktrees on that VM, and session files are pushed to a repo after every turn so another VM can resume them. The cost claim is a break-even: above about 640 session-hours a month, one always-on 4 vCPU VM is cheaper than per-session sandboxes.

mechanism: A small agent proposes several candidate next actions. Two separately trained models then judge them: a simulator that predicts what the tool would return, and a value estimator trained on trajectories labelled by whether the final answer was right. Only the chosen action is executed for real, so rejected candidates cost no tool calls.
claim: GAIA accuracy rises from 13.6% to 41.7% for Qwen3.5-4B and from 22.3% to 50.5% for Qwen3.5-9B.
why_not_testable: It needs trained models and a local language model, and neither is available tonight.
needs: Local model hosting and the trained simulator and value models.
one_line: Seer lets a small research agent imagine tool results with a trained simulator and score them before acting, lifting GAIA from 13.6% to 41.7%.
idea_why: The design is coherent, but the gains are the authors' own on one benchmark family.
breakdown: Collect real search-and-read trajectories with final correctness labels, train a response predictor and a value scorer offline, then wrap a small model so it proposes several actions and only runs the top scored one. The trajectory corpus is the part that needs building or hiring. A cheap proxy is to ask a frontier model to score proposed steps before executing them.
